questions.q: How does the placebo effect produce real relief?
a: The brain releases chemicals like endorphins based on expectation
The treatment contains a small dose of the active drug
The body gradually repairs itself with no outside input
The treatment directly stimulates the immune system
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the brain already holds the chemicals it needs and releases them when it expects relief.

questions.q: In the milkshake study, what happened when both shakes had the same calories?
a: The luxurious label made it taste better and the diet label raised hunger
The full-fat label made people eat less overall
Neither group could tell the two shakes apart
The diet group reported feeling fuller for longer
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the fancier label earned higher taste ratings while the diet label triggered more ghrelin.

questions.q: Which hormone rose in people who believed they were drinking the diet shake?
a: Ghrelin, which signals hunger
Dopamine, which signals reward
Serotonin, which lifts mood
Endorphin, which dulls pain
questions.why: Lesson 2 says ghrelin tells us we are hungry, and expecting fewer calories was enough to raise it.

questions.q: What does lesson 3 say you should understand first before using expectation?
a: Your own personality and the kinds of stories that inspire you
The latest clinical trials on placebo treatments
Your family's full medical history
The going rate for alternative therapies
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to find what captures your individual imagination and suits how suggestible you are.

questions.q: Which warning does the author give about using the power of expectation?
a: Don't abandon proper medical treatment for alternative remedies
Don't discuss your beliefs with your doctor
Don't try hypnosis without a partner present
Don't rely on rituals you invented yourself
questions.why: Lesson 3 says alternative therapies can help but should be used alongside needed medical treatment.
